items.title: Agentic AI Raises New Questions for Financial Institutions
items.summary:
DownloadDownload

Artificial intelligence (AI) has moved beyond answering questions and generating content. Increasingly, AI systems are being designed to act. Agentic AI can pursue objectives, make decisions and take actions on a user’s behalf, potentially with limited human involvement in individual decisions. [...] Consider a customer who gives an AI agent access to a bank account with an instruction to manage the customer’s cash efficiently. The agent decides to transfer funds, convert currencies or purchase an investment.

At first sight, these may appear to be ordinary customer transactions. Agentic AI, however, exposes important distinctions between identity, authentication, authority and attribution. [...] As agentic AI becomes more capable, firms may increasingly encounter interactions in which an AI agent collects information, compares products and initiates transactions for a customer. That creates a new layer between the institution and the person or entity with whom it has established a customer relationship.

items.title: He’s using AI to screen existing compounds for therapeutic potential | University of Pittsburgh
items.summary: Developing pharmaceuticals using AI isn’t new, but it is laborious and often leads to a dead end. “If you generate a brand-new molecule, that’s actually a limitation,” Wang said. “A lot of compounds can’t be synthesized, and that is a big issue.” [...] This back and forth is the GAN’s training. Over time, the generator learns to generate fingerprints that more closely resemble those of real molecules. Researchers then search chemical databases for existing compounds with similar footprints; the AI-generated pattern leads to the discovery of real molecules that researchers can test — no need to synthesize a new molecule. [...] In a paper published Oct. 28 in the journal Science Advances, Wang outlined Full-Spectrum Generative Lead Discovery (FSGLD), a novel, practical and reusable framework that takes advantage of generative AI to screen for existing compounds with potential for therapeutic development.

items.title: Có Nên Học Công Nghệ Thông Tin? Học CNTT Có Khó Không?
items.summary:
## Ai Phù Hợp Với Ngành Công Nghệ Thông Tin?

Ngành Công nghệ thông tin phù hợp với người yêu thích công nghệ, có tư duy logic, kiên trì giải quyết vấn đề và sẵn sàng tự học. Không nhất thiết phải biết lập trình trước khi vào đại học, nhưng học sinh nên có hứng thú tìm hiểu cách các hệ thống máy tính và ứng dụng hoạt động.

### Những Tố Chất Phù Hợp Với Ngành CNTT

Dưới đy là một số đặc điểm có thể giúp học sinh học tập và phát triển trong ngành. [...] Có nên học Công nghệ thông tin? Học CNTT có khó không? Đy là những băn khoăn phổ biến của học sinh THPT khi đứng trước lựa chọn ngành học. Công nghệ thông tin (CNTT) vẫn có nhiều hướng nghề nghiệp trong lĩnh vực phần mềm, dữ liệu, bảo mật và hệ thống máy tính. Tuy nhiên, ngành học này đòi hỏi khả năng tư duy logic, kiên trì thực hành và chủ động cập nhật kiến thức. Để quyết định có nên học CNTT, học sinh cần nhìn nhận thực tế thị trường việc làm, độ khó của chương trình và mức độ phù hợp với [...] Nên học Công nghệ thông tin nếu bạn yêu thích công nghệ, có khả năng tư duy logic và sẵn sàng dành thời gian học tập, thực hành lu dài. Ngành CNTT phù hợp với người muốn sử dụng máy tính và phần mềm để giải quyết vấn đề thực tế, không chỉ với những học sinh đã biết lập trình từ THPT.

Tuy nhiên, quyết định chọn ngành cần dựa trên sở thích, năng lực và mục tiêu nghề nghiệp thay vì kỳ vọng rằng học CNTT chắc chắn có thu nhập cao.

### Những Lý Do Nên Cn Nhắc Ngành Công Nghệ Thông Tin

results.input: Giải giúp mình bài toán tích phân: nguyên hàm của x^2 là gì?

result.actual_text:
Để tìm nguyên hàm của \( x^2 \), chúng ta cần tìm một hàm \( F(x) \) sao cho \( F'(x) = x^2 \).

Đây là một bài toán tích phân đơn giản. Nguyên hàm của \( x^2 \) là:

\[ F(x) = \frac{x^3}{3} + C \]

Trong đó \( C \) là hằng số integrating constant. 

Vậy, nguyên hàm của \( x^2 \) là \( \frac{x^3}{3} + C \). 

Bạn cần biết thêm thông tin nào khác không?

They want to build an agentic business,” said Mohamad Ali, Senior Vice President and Head of IBM Consulting. “Microsoft and IBM are helping organizations bring human expertise and digital labor together in a way that can scale across the enterprise, to turn AI from a productivity aid into a real competitive advantage.” [...] “AI is evolving quickly, and our focus at SEI is on applying it with intention in ways that strengthen trust, enhance human decision-making and create meaningful value across our business,” said Sneha Shah, Chief AI Strategist and Head of SEI Next. “Our work with IBM Consulting and Microsoft is helping us explore how emerging capabilities could support critical processes and be responsibly scaled over time, with the goal to create better experiences for our employees and clients. By combining [...] “Enterprise AI will be won by organizations that can turn their data, industry expertise and AI into action,” said Rodrigo Kede Lima, President, Microsoft Frontier Company. “Together, Microsoft and IBM Consulting are bringing the best of our technology and expertise, to help customers move from AI ambition to business impact faster and with confidence.”

items.title: Fall Staff Town Hall highlights ‘human-centered AI,’ community partnerships | Latest | NDWorks | University of Notre Dame
items.summary:
McGreevy highlighted Notre Dame's opportunities to use AI to advance research, particularly through the Data, AI, and Computing Initiative, led by Nitesh Chawla, the Frank M. Freimann Professor of Computer Science and Engineering and Lucy Family Director for AI & Academic Strategy, as well as the University’s growing strength in AI ethics, including the work of Meghan Sullivan, the Wilsey Family College Professor of Philosophy and founding director of the Institute for Ethics and the Common [...] From the staff perspective, Cullinan said AI presents opportunities to work more efficiently and better steward the University's resources. But those efforts would remain “human-centered," a dynamic he said might seem contradictory at other universities.

“Not at Notre Dame,” Cullinan said. “I think the most important asset that we have, and will have, is our people.” [...] “What will set our students apart is their competency in interpersonal skills: their ability to make moral judgments, to recognize injustice, and to work on addressing that," he said.

McGreevy echoed Father Dowd's characterization of a "bilingual" education, saying students should still be challenged even as AI makes some assignments easier.

items.title: He’s using AI to screen existing compounds for therapeutic potential | University of Pittsburgh
items.summary: Developing pharmaceuticals using AI isn’t new, but it is laborious and often leads to a dead end. “If you generate a brand-new molecule, that’s actually a limitation,” Wang said. “A lot of compounds can’t be synthesized, and that is a big issue.” [...] This back and forth is the GAN’s training. Over time, the generator learns to generate fingerprints that more closely resemble those of real molecules. Researchers then search chemical databases for existing compounds with similar footprints; the AI-generated pattern leads to the discovery of real molecules that researchers can test — no need to synthesize a new molecule. [...] In a paper published Oct. 28 in the journal Science Advances, Wang outlined Full-Spectrum Generative Lead Discovery (FSGLD), a novel, practical and reusable framework that takes advantage of generative AI to screen for existing compounds with potential for therapeutic development.

items.title: Practice Makes Precise: At CoRL, NVIDIA and Partners Reveal How Robots Rehearse Delicate Work in Simulation | NVIDIA Blog
items.summary:
“To me, agentic robotics is the most exciting technological development since the internet in 1995,” said Ken Goldberg, professor of robotics at UC Berkeley and a lead on the VABAR and GaP projects.

Ambi Robotics is exploring GaP for industrial automation.

Ambi Robotics, Bosch Research and Siemens are all exploring GaP for its agentic robotics workflows across diverse industrial scenarios.

Learn more by joining NVIDIA at CoRL.

 Categories:
 Robotics [...] The shift from locomotion to manipulation is taking center stage at this week’s Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL) in Austin, Texas, alongside the rise of agentic robotics — a new paradigm that integrates frontier agents to create interpretable code for physical robotics systems.

At CoRL, NVIDIA is introducing new open robotics technologies, including world action models, simulation tools, benchmarks and agentic workflows. [...] Walden Robotics is using Isaac Sim’s photorealistic rendering to train and evaluate its general-purpose robot in virtual environments for manufacturing and logistics, while Dexmate is exploring how coding agents can rehearse and refine manipulation strategies in Isaac Sim before executing them on its Vega robot.

items.title: Pulkit Agrawal (Eka Robotics): Why Robots Need Practice to Master the Physical World | Physical AI
items.summary:
MIT associate professor and Eka Robotics cofounder Pulkit Agrawal explains the difference between planning a task and physically executing it. He argues that broader skills must be matched by speed, precision and reliability before robots become products people want to use. [...] ### Transcript
[0:00] [music]
[0:07] I'll tell you a bit about what we are doing at EKA. So if you think about robotics, I think there are two problems that need to be solved, right? One problem is planning, another is control.
[0:17] So suppose you tell a robot, make me dinner. It needs to, you know, go to the fridge [snorts] and figure out what vegetables to take out, keep them on the [...] [10:58] by trial and error. And because these systems could do trial and error for billions and billions of examples, they mastered these things and found strategies which are better than humans.
[11:08] But if we want to bring these ideas into robotics, there is a big problem. You know, imagine if you put a robot in the
[11:16] real world and it has to go practice things. You know, it's going to break itself. It's going to break objects.
